# Trace both backend selection and native handler registration

## Platform difference

Dart adapters and native host files do not establish a working platform call unless the selected backend is installed and its matching native handler is attached.

## Implementation

Kazumi repairs wakelock by adding its native plugin registration. Shuqi registers a limited set of OH plugins while retained battery/WebView/share calls exceed that set; an override for device_info_plus also does not replace imports of legacy device_info. OronBox has Dart BLE/SPP channel adapters, but its study found neither installation of the OH BLE adapter nor matching native handlers in tracked source. Nomark explicitly registers its app-owned native plugin despite an empty generated registrar.

## Applicability

This applies to package plugins, federated Dart implementations and application-owned channels. The cited Kazumi manual registrant edit is historical evidence; for a generated package registrant, repair generator inputs rather than treating hand edits as a universal workflow.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

A scan of tracked source cannot establish what an unavailable proprietary or local artifact implements. OronBox pairing success stubs and false query results must not be interpreted as verified Bluetooth operations.

## Verification

Follow a public API through backend selection, messenger/channel names and native handlers. Exercise success, unsupported methods and missing-plugin behavior on the actual engine.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
